questions.stem: MFA requires at least two factors from:

choices.C: A username and a security question
choices.D: Something you know, something you have, and/or something you are

questions.explanation: MFA combines two or more independent factor categories. Using two factors from the same category is not true MFA.

questions.stem: TOTP codes expire after ~30 seconds to:

choices.B: Make stolen codes useless after a very brief window

questions.explanation: TOTP codes are time-based and expire quickly, a code intercepted from one session cannot be reused in a different time window.

questions.stem: FIDO2 hardware keys are most phishing-resistant because:

choices.A: They generate very long OTP codes
choices.B: They encrypt the entire TLS session
choices.C: They bind authentication to the specific registered origin domain, refusing to authenticate to phishing sites
choices.D: They require a biometric scan in addition to the key press

questions.explanation: FIDO2 keys use public-key cryptography bound to the registered origin. A phishing site cannot obtain a valid response because the origin doesn't match.

choices.C: SQL injection on the login form

questions.explanation: Account lockout caps authentication attempts, making automated brute-force and credential stuffing attacks impractical.

choices.C: Rainbow table attacks using precomputed hash tables
choices.D: Credential stuffing with stolen plaintext passwords

questions.explanation: A salt is a random value appended to a password before hashing. Unique per-password salts make precomputed rainbow tables useless.

choices.A: Using a captured NTLM hash directly to authenticate without knowing the plaintext password
choices.C: Replacing a stored hash with a malicious one
choices.D: Cracking a hash using a rainbow table

questions.explanation: Pass-the-hash captures a Windows NTLM hash and authenticates to other systems using it directly, no plaintext password needed.

choices.C: Mandatory periodic password rotation on a fixed schedule

questions.explanation: NIST found mandatory rotation leads to predictable patterns (Password1! → Password2!). Rotation should occur only when compromise is suspected.

choices.A: Administrators have standing admin rights on all servers
choices.B: All admin tasks must complete within one hour
choices.C: Privileges are granted only for an approved time window and auto-revoked when the task is complete
choices.D: Privileged accounts are created instantly when needed

questions.explanation: JIT minimises standing privileges. Admin rights are granted for a specific window and automatically revoked, limiting damage from compromised credentials.

choices.B: Automatically rotating session tokens every minute
choices.D: Allowing one authenticated session to access multiple systems, reducing password fatigue and reuse

questions.explanation: SSO means users authenticate once. Fewer passwords means less reuse and fewer weak passwords on individual systems.

choices.A: Any workstation with a complex password
choices.B: An encrypted vault for storing privileged credentials
choices.C: A remote desktop gateway for all admin connections
choices.D: A hardened dedicated workstation used only for privileged administrative tasks, isolated from internet and email

questions.explanation: A PAW is isolated from the internet and email, preventing admin credentials from being compromised via phishing or malware on a general-use workstation.
